source_snapshot.script: No Script; ten attended and ten machine minutes.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES; keeps six lines after a case-insensitive RIO text match from OOB FRU output, exposes the password and calls the result full/no-risk.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION; treats RIO as remote-I/O, requires board/attached-I/O mapping, complete inventory, expected fields, Web parity and non-disturbance evidence.

historical_reviews.deepseek: The RIO filter is only a tentative locator; it can miss vendor naming or match unrelated text and truncates the record. It supplies no authoritative expansion of RIO or field oracle.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Its conditional classification and protected collection are sound, but `remote-I/O` must remain a project-confirmed meaning rather than an inferred expansion of the acronym.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Earlier RIO_BD management-bus cases validate a logical route, not board FRU data; their map may be correlated only after the owner confirms the same assembly.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-04/34 allow component meaning, topology and expected fields as project inputs; ED-38 preserves evidence/state and engineer verdict ownership.

original_test_intent: Validate the board-level FRU record for the assembly designated RIO BD by this project, including correct identity/service fields and the matching BMC-Web object, without assuming what RIO expands to or exercising attached interfaces.
original_method: The owner defines the RIO board's function, physical location and revision, maps it to a stable FRU device and Web object, supplies expected fields, then the agent captures the complete inventory and performs a passive comparison while checking that associated management or I/O health did not change.
manual_activity: The platform owner defines RIO for this design, identifies the exact board and attached-interface domain, maps its FRU/Web records and judges field mismatches. Automation does not manipulate any RIO-connected interface.
required_inputs: Authoritative RIO acronym/function and board physical location
RIO board PN/revision/serial and parent/attached-interface topology
Stable FRU device/area and exact BMC-Web object
Allowed optional, blank, placeholder, encoding and normalization rules
Relationship, if any, to other RIO_BD I2C/hardware source rows
Baseline interface/BMC/SEL/OS health and independent recovery owner
safety_requirements: Do not infer that RIO means remote-I/O until the project confirms it
Do not borrow a bus-route result as FRU identity evidence
Retain the complete FRU inventory before extracting a mapped record
Do not actuate external I/O, change pin state, rescan/reset links, write FRU or update firmware
Preserve existing SEL and OS logs rather than clearing them automatically
Protect BMC credentials and retain redacted raw evidence
Stop on target ambiguity, duplicate/missing record, interface-state change, BMC instability or unexpected events
agent_execution_scope: Verify source and owner-approved RIO board identity
Record passive associated-interface and management health
Collect the complete raw FRU inventory through approved access
Resolve the board record by stable device/area and compare all required fields
Prepare the exact Web record for operator confirmation
Perform no I/O control, write, reset, firmware or verdict action
engineer_actions: Define RIO function/location and board applicability
Approve board-to-FRU/Web mapping and expected fields
State whether related RIO rows cover the same or distinct assembly
Resolve anomalies and issue the result

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `fru print` is a relevant passive source, but `grep -iA6 RIO` is neither a stable device selector nor a complete record. It cannot define the board, compare Web/expected fields or protect against false matches and it exposes the password in argv.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Using approved secret-safe BMC access, archive the complete FRU inventory, select the owner-mapped RIO board by stable FRU identity, compare its entire approved field set and correlate the exact Web object without operating attached interfaces.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: RIO BD, `fru list`, readability/correctness/Web criteria and 10/10-minute estimates remain; no acronym expansion, topology or control action is invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES RIO DEFINITION, BOARD MAP AND FRU ORACLE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the project-specific RIO board to a physical location and FRU device, compare complete board fields with service truth, confirm Web parity and use only passive interface health to prove non-disturbance.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves the ambiguous acronym through project data and replaces name-only filtering with stable board provenance.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A readable RIO string cannot prove which assembly or its full identity; an I2C response or live attached interface demonstrates connectivity, not FRU correctness.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The inventory read is low impact, but misidentifying a board that owns external or fabric I/O could direct later service or recovery to the wrong interface domain.

project_override_considerations: If RIO is integrated or project-specific, record its actual owning assembly and applicability. The project may correlate another row's map only with an explicit identity link; it may not merge distinct atomic results.
expected_evidence: Exact source/variant and approved RIO definition/function/location
RIO board PN/revision/serial and attached-domain topology
Stable FRU device/area and BMC-Web mapping
Complete redacted raw FRU output and exit status
Mapped full record plus false/missing/duplicate analysis
Web parity and before/after passive associated-interface/BMC/SEL/OS health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master row consistently asks for the FRU of a board named RIO BD. The acronym and expected values are undefined, but no incompatible method or criterion appears within the row.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operation remains a standard passive board-FRU comparison. Authoritative board meaning, mapping and field truth are normal project inputs, so execution can be bounded once provided.

review_improvement: Prevents an inferred acronym or related I2C record from defining the board, requires stable RIO provenance and confines interface evidence to non-disturbance rather than FRU acceptance.
independent_technical_reasoning: RIO is not self-defining across platforms, so the first engineering obligation is component identity, not command selection. Once the owner binds that label to a board and FRU device, full inventory and Web fields can be compared safely. A six-line name match or bus response could succeed for a different object, while active I/O manipulation would exceed this row's passive FRU scope.
